rounds.fact: Encyclopedia Britannica put its entire encyclopedia online for free in 1999, a bold bet that ad revenue could replace its centuries-old subscription business, before pulling back a year later.
BuzzFeed started in 2006 as an experiment in tracking what content spreads virally online, well before its listicle format became one of the most imitated web formats of the 2010s.
Blizzard's late-90s site supported both Diablo and StarCraft, two games that helped define entire genres and whose online play features were unusually ambitious for their time.
Instagram launched iPhone-only in late 2010 and hit 25,000 users on day one. Its web presence stayed minimal for years while the app itself was the whole product.
Delicious (originally styled del.icio.us) popularized social bookmarking and the very concept of a 'tag,' letting users save and label links for themselves and everyone else to browse.
